title: One Oxygen. One Biology. One BHOC System.
intro: Species differ. Blood systems differ. But the biological need for oxygen is universal. The BHOC Initiative applies comparative biology and veterinary evidence to support species protection across the living world.
pathwayLabel: Conceptual oxygen-delivery cascade from the lungs to mitochondria

image.alt: Black line schematic of the lungs

steps.title: Oxygen enters the lungs
steps.text: Gas exchange moves oxygen from inhaled air into pulmonary blood.

image.alt: Black line schematic of blood cells

steps.title: Blood carries oxygen
steps.text: Erythrocytes carry oxygen. BHOC is designed to carry oxygen in plasma.

image.alt: Black line schematic of a vital organ

steps.title: Blood reaches the organ
steps.text: Circulation brings oxygen toward organ tissue and its microvasculature.

image.alt: Black line schematic of a biological cell

steps.title: Oxygen reaches the cell
steps.text: Oxygen moves from the microcirculation through tissue to cells.

image.alt: Black line schematic of a mitochondrion

steps.title: Mitochondria use oxygen
steps.text: Mitochondria use oxygen in aerobic metabolism to support ATP production.

evidenceBoundary.label: Evidence boundary:
evidenceBoundary.text: Veterinary evidence is product and species specific. Historical Oxyglobin approvals and study outcomes do not establish BHOC approval or efficacy across species. The current veterinary index contains 236 bibliographic records, including 235 source-linked citations.
